articles.title: How Beijing's 12345 forum reshapes global talks on urban governance

articles.summaryCn: 本文通过作者亲历12345热线的深夜求助经历，介绍了北京“接诉即办”机制从市长热线到城市治理平台的发展历程、运行规模及其在国际论坛上引发的全球关注与借鉴意义。

paragraphs.en: About a week ago, at around midnight, I was {{0}} awake by a loud noise. Living next to railway tracks, I am no stranger to the occasional {{1}}. But this one was loud enough to wake me even with earplugs in. So I called the only number I knew could help: the hotline for swift response to public complaints, 12345. The {{2}} politely confirmed my location and told me that someone would get back to me within a few minutes.
paragraphs.cn: 大约一周前，午夜时分，我被一声巨响惊醒。住在铁路旁，我对偶尔的隆隆声并不陌生。但这一次的声音大到即使戴着耳塞也能把我吵醒。于是我拨通了我所知道的唯一能帮忙的号码：快速响应公众诉求的热线——12345。接线员礼貌地确认了我的位置，并告诉我几分钟内会有人回复我。

paragraphs.en: Five minutes later, I received a call. I was told that urgent {{3}} work was being carried out on the railway tracks and was given an {{4}} of how much longer it would continue. And, almost like clockwork, the noise stopped when the stated time was up. I went back to sleep, but the experience stayed with me. Not simply because my immediate problem had been addressed, but because of the system behind that seemingly ordinary phone call.
paragraphs.cn: 五分钟后，我接到了一通电话。我被告知铁路轨道正在进行紧急维修，并得到了维修还将持续多久的估计。几乎像钟表一样准时，噪音在所说的时间到时停止了。我重新入睡，但这次经历留在了我的心里。不仅仅因为我眼前的问题得到了解决，更因为那通看似普通的电话背后所支撑的系统。

paragraphs.en:

China's government hotlines have a history stretching back several decades. paragraphs.en: In Beijing, the hotline has evolved into something much larger than a telephone service. The city's "Swift Response to Public Complaints" {{8}}, launched in 2019, places 12345 at the center of a broader governance system designed around rapid response, efficient handling, timely feedback and, increasingly, {{9}} problem-solving. The scale of Beijing's 12345 system is {{10}}. Over the seven years since the launch of the reform in 2019, the platform has handled {{11}} 200 million requests, including inquiries, complaints, requests for assistance and suggestions. paragraphs.cn: 在北京，这条热线已经发展成为一个远不止电话服务的更大事物。该市于2019年启动的“接诉即办”机制，将12345置于一个更广泛的治理体系的中心，该体系围绕快速响应、高效办理、及时反馈以及日益主动的问题解决而设计。北京12345系统的规模令人瞩目。自2019年改革启动以来的七年间，该平台已处理了约2亿件诉求，包括咨询、投诉、求助和建议。根据市政府发布的《2025年度数据分析报告》，该热线在2025年处理了2580.2万件来自居民和企业的诉求，比上年增长了6.6%。

That amounts to approximately 70,700 requests a day. This is where the principle often summarized as "the street whistles, the department responds" becomes more than a slogan. It reflects an effort to connect residents' concerns with the government departments responsible for addressing them, without requiring residents to navigate the administrative structure themselves. Issues such as housing, transport, employment, consumer protection and access to public services often require {{12}} across multiple departments and levels of administration.

Held under the core concept of "People's City, Better Life," this year's forum, taking place on October 12 and 13, brings discussions on urban governance closer to residents by extending exchanges into communities and frontline governance settings. More than 3,200 participants are attending, including over 240 international guests from more than 70 countries and regions. I spoke with three visiting journalists from Hungary, North Macedonia and Namibia to hear what stood out to them and which aspects of Beijing's approach they thought might be relevant to their own countries. Mihály Zsiros, a Hungarian TV host and reporter who had been in Beijing for just over a month, said he had first learned about the 12345 hotline at the forum and considered the concept particularly useful for a megacity of Beijing's size. Separating non-emergency inquiries from emergency calls, he argued, could help ensure that emergency operators remain available to focus on urgent cases. paragraphs.en: Sallai said he was learning about Beijing's 12345 hotline for the first time. In North Macedonia, residents can contact their respective municipalities through local telephone numbers or visit municipal offices in person to raise concerns. However, he explained, the arrangements are {{14}}, and municipal contact numbers do not always function effectively. "What really impressed me was that [residents] have the opportunity to be heard by government," he said, referring to Beijing's population of more than 20 million. Drawing a comparison with smaller municipalities in North Macedonia, he said residents' concerns could sometimes take considerable time to address, even when they were brought to the attention of local authorities.
paragraphs.cn: Sallai说他是第一次了解北京的12345热线。在北马其顿，居民可以通过当地电话号码联系各自所在的城市，或亲自前往市政办公室反映问题。然而，他解释说，这些安排是分散的，市政联系电话并不总能有效运作。“真正让我印象深刻的是，（居民）有机会被政府听到，”他说，指的是北京超过2000万的人口。与北马其顿较小的城市相比，他说，居民的关切有时即使被地方当局注意到，也可能需要相当长的时间才能得到解决。

Sallai also cautioned that establishing a system on the scale of Beijing's would require {{15}} commitment and investment. "For these things to happen, it's needed [for] the whole government to take [them] seriously and to take action," he said. Rousa Shikoha, a senior producer in the News and Current Affairs department of the Namibian Broadcasting Corporation, said she had researched Beijing's 12345 hotline before visiting China, but the forum had given her a clearer understanding of how it operates. She described the approach as impressive and said it illustrated China's emphasis on people-centered urban development.
paragraphs.cn: Sallai还提醒说，建立像北京这样规模的系统需要大量的承诺和投入。“要让这些事情发生，需要整个政府认真对待（它们）并采取行动，”他说。Rousa Shikoha是纳米比亚广播公司新闻与时事部的高级制片人，她说她在访问中国之前就研究过北京的12345热线，但论坛让她对其运作方式有了更清晰的了解。来自全球南方的媒体代表参观北京市民热线服务中心，实地了解该系统如何运作以及数字和智能技术如何应用于公共服务，10月9日，北京。Zaruhi Poghosyan。她称这一做法令人印象深刻，并表示它体现了中国对以人为本的城市发展的重视。

paragraphs.en: Namibia also has channels through which residents can raise public-service concerns, Shikoha explained. Municipal councils provide help desks for inquiries, while the capital, Windhoek, has separate contact points for municipal matters and city-police services. Emergency services and other public functions are organized separately rather than through a single centralized hub. For Shikoha, one of the most relevant aspects of Beijing's model was its use of technology to support frontline staff. "What I think we would like to incorporate is the digital technological aspect of it," she said, noting that Namibia does not currently use AI to support staff in the same way she had observed in Beijing.
paragraphs.cn: Shikoha解释说，纳米比亚也有居民可以反映公共服务问题的渠道。市政委员会设有咨询求助台，而首都温得和克则分别设有处理市政事务和城市警察服务的联系点。紧急服务和其他公共职能是分开组织的，而不是通过一个单一的集中枢纽。对Shikoha来说，北京模式中最相关的方面之一是利用技术支持一线工作人员。“我认为我们希望纳入的是它的数字技术方面，”她说，并指出纳米比亚目前并不像她在北京看到的那样使用人工智能来支持员工。

paragraphs.en:
She suggested that technology could help reduce employees' workloads, improve efficiency and enable public services to respond to residents more quickly. Digital tools, she added, could {{16}} operations and make it easier for people to receive timely responses. The three journalists approached Beijing's system from different perspectives: separating emergency calls from non-emergency requests, ensuring that residents' concerns reach government, and using technology to improve public-service delivery. Their observations point to a broader consideration for cities interested in similar approaches: the technology and administrative structures may differ, but an effective complaint-handling system requires accessible channels, clear responsibilities and a commitment to follow through. Beyond the hotline
For Beijing, the challenge extends beyond receiving complaints and responding to them.
paragraphs.cn: 她建议，技术可以帮助减轻员工的工作量、提高效率，并使公共服务能够更快地回应居民。她补充说，数字工具可以简化运营，让人们更容易及时得到回复。这三位记者从不同角度看待北京的系统：将紧急呼叫与非紧急请求分开、确保居民的关切传达到政府，以及利用技术改善公共服务供给。他们的观察指向了有意采取类似做法的城市需要更广泛考虑的一点：技术和行政结构可能不同，但一个有效的投诉处理系统需要可及的渠道、明确的职责以及坚持到底的承诺。超越热线。对北京来说，挑战不仅在于接收投诉并作出回应。

paragraphs.en: The aim is increasingly to use the information generated by millions of requests to identify recurring problems, improve public services and address issues before they prompt further complaints. Over the seven years since the reform began, Beijing reports that its resolution rate rose from 53.1% to 97.3%, while its satisfaction rate increased from 64.6% to 97.7%, according to the municipal government's 2025 report. These figures help illustrate the development of the hotline and its central role in the city's approach to governance. My midnight encounter with 12345 was a small interaction with a very large system. I called because I wanted to know why I was being kept awake.
paragraphs.cn: 目标日益在于利用数百万件诉求所产生的信息来识别反复出现的问题、改善公共服务，并在问题引发更多投诉之前加以解决。根据市政府的2025年报告，自改革开始以来的七年间，北京报告其解决率从53.1%上升到97.3%，而满意率从64.6%上升到97.7%。这些数字有助于说明这条热线的发展及其在城市治理方式中的核心作用。我午夜与12345的接触，是与一个非常庞大系统的一次小小互动。我打电话是因为我想知道我为什么一直睡不着。

paragraphs.en: Someone listened, found the relevant information, called me back and gave me an answer. For one resident on one night, that was enough. But the larger significance of the system lies in what happens when millions of such interactions are collected, assessed and used to inform decisions. Beijing's experience offers a surprisingly revealing window into China's people-centered governance logic, while raising questions relevant to cities elsewhere: How can residents make their concerns heard? How can public institutions respond effectively?
paragraphs.cn: 有人倾听了，找到了相关信息，给我回了电话，并给了我一个答复。对某位居民在某个夜晚来说，这就足够了。但该系统的更大意义在于，当数百万次这样的互动被收集、评估并用于为决策提供依据时会发生什么。北京的经验为了解中国以人为本的治理逻辑提供了一个出人意料地具有揭示性的窗口，同时提出了与其他地方城市相关的问题：居民如何让自己的关切被听到？公共机构如何有效回应？

paragraphs.en: And how can the lessons from individual complaints be used to prevent similar problems from recurring? Ultimately, good governance begins by listening to the people, is tested by solving their problems and gains legitimacy by improving their lives. Editor's note: Zaruhi Poghosyan is a multimedia editor for CGTN Digital. This article is part of a series on Beijing's evolving digital services for locals and international visitors alike.

Sallai said he was learning about Beijing's 12345 hotline for the first time. In North Macedonia, residents can contact their respective municipalities through local telephone numbers or visit municipal offices in person to raise concerns. However, he explained, the arrangements are decentralized, and municipal contact numbers do not always function effectively.
"What really impressed me was that [residents] have the opportunity to be heard by government," he said, referring to Beijing's population of more than 20 million.
Drawing a comparison with smaller municipalities in North Macedonia, he said residents' concerns could sometimes take considerable time to address, even when they were brought to the attention of local authorities.
Sallai also cautioned that establishing a system on the scale of Beijing's would require substantial commitment and investment.
"For these things to happen, it's needed [for] the whole government to take [them] seriously and to take action," he said.
Rousa Shikoha, a senior producer in the News and Current Affairs department of the Namibian Broadcasting Corporation, said she had researched Beijing's 12345 hotline before visiting China, but the forum had given her a clearer understanding of how it operates.
Media representatives from the Global South visit the Beijing Citizen Hotline Service Center to learn firsthand how the system operates and how digital and intelligent technologies are being applied to public services, October 9, Beijing. Zaruhi Poghosyan
She described the approach as impressive and said it illustrated China's emphasis on people-centered urban development.
Namibia also has channels through which residents can raise public-service concerns, Shikoha explained. Municipal councils provide help desks for inquiries, while the capital, Windhoek, has separate contact points for municipal matters and city-police services. Emergency services and other public functions are organized separately rather than through a single centralized hub.
For Shikoha, one of the most relevant aspects of Beijing's model was its use of technology to support frontline staff.
"What I think we would like to incorporate is the digital technological aspect of it," she said, noting that Namibia does not currently use AI to support staff in the same way she had observed in Beijing.
She suggested that technology could help reduce employees' workloads, improve efficiency and enable public services to respond to residents more quickly. Digital tools, she added, could streamline operations and make it easier for people to receive timely responses.
The three journalists approached Beijing's system from different perspectives: separating emergency calls from non-emergency requests, ensuring that residents' concerns reach government, and using technology to improve public-service delivery. Their observations point to a broader consideration for cities interested in similar approaches: the technology and administrative structures may differ, but an effective complaint-handling system requires accessible channels, clear responsibilities and a commitment to follow through.
Beyond the hotline
For Beijing, the challenge extends beyond receiving complaints and responding to them. The aim is increasingly to use the information generated by millions of requests to identify recurring problems, improve public services and address issues before they prompt further complaints.
Over the seven years since the reform began, Beijing reports that its resolution rate rose from 53.1% to 97.3%, while its satisfaction rate increased from 64.6% to 97.7%, according to the municipal government's 2025 report.
These figures help illustrate the development of the hotline and its central role in the city's approach to governance.
My midnight encounter with 12345 was a small interaction with a very large system. I called because I wanted to know why I was being kept awake. Someone listened, found the relevant information, called me back and gave me an answer. For one resident on one night, that was enough.
But the larger significance of the system lies in what happens when millions of such interactions are collected, assessed and used to inform decisions.
Beijing's experience offers a surprisingly revealing window into China's people-centered governance logic, while raising questions relevant to cities elsewhere: How can residents make their concerns heard? How can public institutions respond effectively? And how can the lessons from individual complaints be used to prevent similar problems from recurring?
Ultimately, good governance begins by listening to the people, is tested by solving their problems and gains legitimacy by improving their lives.
Editor's note: Zaruhi Poghosyan is a multimedia editor for CGTN Digital. This article is part of a series on Beijing's evolving digital services for locals and international visitors alike.

大约一周前，午夜时分，我被一声巨响惊醒。住在铁路旁，我对偶尔的隆隆声并不陌生。但这一次的声音大到即使戴着耳塞也能把我吵醒。于是我拨通了我所知道的唯一能帮忙的号码：快速响应公众诉求的热线——12345。接线员礼貌地确认了我的位置，并告诉我几分钟内会有人回复我。

五分钟后，我接到了一通电话。我被告知铁路轨道正在进行紧急维修，并得到了维修还将持续多久的估计。几乎像钟表一样准时，噪音在所说的时间到时停止了。我重新入睡，但这次经历留在了我的心里。不仅仅因为我眼前的问题得到了解决，更因为那通看似普通的电话背后所支撑的系统。

于是我决定深入了解一座拥有超过2000万人口的城市如何将个人的投诉、问题和请求转化为具体的政府行动。一条热线又能揭示一座城市怎样的治理方式？从市长热线到全市治理平台，中国的政府热线已有数十年的历史。一些城市在20世纪80年代开始推出被称为“市长热线”的服务，为居民提供直接向地方当局反映问题的渠道。随着时间的推移，各城市发展并整合了其公共服务热线，12345成为非紧急政府服务的统一号码。

在北京，这条热线已经发展成为一个远不止电话服务的更大事物。该市于2019年启动的“接诉即办”机制，将12345置于一个更广泛的治理体系的中心，该体系围绕快速响应、高效办理、及时反馈以及日益主动的问题解决而设计。北京12345系统的规模令人瞩目。自2019年改革启动以来的七年间，该平台已处理了约2亿件诉求，包括咨询、投诉、求助和建议。根据市政府发布的《2025年度数据分析报告》，该热线在2025年处理了2580.2万件来自居民和企业的诉求，比上年增长了6.6%。

这相当于每天约70700件诉求。这正是常被概括为“街乡吹哨、部门报到”的原则不再只是一句口号的地方。它反映了一种努力，即将居民的关切与负责解决这些问题的政府部门连接起来，而无需居民自己去应对行政架构。分享经验，探索解决方案。随着城市扩张和城市生活日益复杂，居民与地方政府之间的关系也在发生变化。住房、交通、就业、消费者保护和公共服务获取等问题往往需要跨多个部门和行政层级的协调。

一个单一的联系点为居民提供了一种应对这种复杂性的方式。但像北京这样的城市的经验，能否为其他面临类似挑战的城市中心提供有益的启示？2026年北京接诉即办论坛于2026年10月12日在中国北京开幕。没有一种可以原封不动地从一座城市移植到另一座城市的普遍模式。行政体系、政治制度、公共服务职责和公民参与渠道差异很大。

然而，根本性的挑战是普遍共有的：确保居民有可及的途径来反映关切，并确保这些关切得到适当的回应。北京一直寻求通过接诉即办论坛与中国以外的地方分享经验，该论坛于2024年首次举办。今年的论坛以“人民城市，美好生活”为核心理念，于10月12日至13日举行，通过将交流延伸到社区和基层治理场景，使关于城市治理的讨论更贴近居民。超过3200名参会者出席，其中包括来自70多个国家和地区的240多名国际嘉宾。论坛将发布一系列研究成果，包括关于“接诉即办”改革的理论研究、关于中国及世界各地城市热线服务与治理成效的评估报告，以及全球城市治理典型案例集。

嘉宾出席2026年北京接诉即办论坛开幕式，中国北京，2026年10月12日。/接诉即办论坛。论坛开幕前，来自全球南方的记者和媒体代表参观了北京市民热线服务中心，实地了解该系统如何运作，以及数字和智能技术如何应用于公共服务。我与三位分别来自匈牙利、北马其顿和纳米比亚的来访记者交谈，听取他们印象最深的地方，以及他们认为北京做法中哪些方面可能与其本国相关。Mihály Zsiros是一位匈牙利电视主持人和记者，他来北京仅一个多月，他说他是在论坛上第一次了解到12345热线，并认为这一概念对像北京这样规模的超大城市特别有用。他指出，匈牙利首都布达佩斯的人口不到200万，而北京的人口超过2000万。

尽管匈牙利有可通过112拨打的专门紧急服务，Zsiros仍认为设立一个单独的非紧急公众咨询和投诉渠道很有价值。他解释说，人们有时会就无需紧急干预的事项联系紧急接线员，这可能会占用他们的时间，而此时其他人正需要立即援助。“我确实认为这是个好主意，”Zsiros说，并建议在匈牙利和其他国家，一个专门的非紧急公众咨询和投诉渠道可能会有用。他认为，将非紧急咨询与紧急呼叫分开，有助于确保紧急接线员能够继续专注于紧急案件。对于来自北马其顿的记者兼电视主持人Valon Sallai来说，最引人注目的方面是居民有机会让政府听到他们的关切。

Sallai说他是第一次了解北京的12345热线。在北马其顿，居民可以通过当地电话号码联系各自所在的城市，或亲自前往市政办公室反映问题。然而，他解释说，这些安排是分散的，市政联系电话并不总能有效运作。“真正让我印象深刻的是，（居民）有机会被政府听到，”他说，指的是北京超过2000万的人口。与北马其顿较小的城市相比，他说，居民的关切有时即使被地方当局注意到，也可能需要相当长的时间才能得到解决。

Sallai还提醒说，建立像北京这样规模的系统需要大量的承诺和投入。“要让这些事情发生，需要整个政府认真对待（它们）并采取行动，”他说。Rousa Shikoha是纳米比亚广播公司新闻与时事部的高级制片人，她说她在访问中国之前就研究过北京的12345热线，但论坛让她对其运作方式有了更清晰的了解。来自全球南方的媒体代表参观北京市民热线服务中心，实地了解该系统如何运作以及数字和智能技术如何应用于公共服务，10月9日，北京。Zaruhi Poghosyan。她称这一做法令人印象深刻，并表示它体现了中国对以人为本的城市发展的重视。

Shikoha解释说，纳米比亚也有居民可以反映公共服务问题的渠道。市政委员会设有咨询求助台，而首都温得和克则分别设有处理市政事务和城市警察服务的联系点。紧急服务和其他公共职能是分开组织的，而不是通过一个单一的集中枢纽。对Shikoha来说，北京模式中最相关的方面之一是利用技术支持一线工作人员。“我认为我们希望纳入的是它的数字技术方面，”她说，并指出纳米比亚目前并不像她在北京看到的那样使用人工智能来支持员工。

她建议，技术可以帮助减轻员工的工作量、提高效率，并使公共服务能够更快地回应居民。她补充说，数字工具可以简化运营，让人们更容易及时得到回复。这三位记者从不同角度看待北京的系统：将紧急呼叫与非紧急请求分开、确保居民的关切传达到政府，以及利用技术改善公共服务供给。他们的观察指向了有意采取类似做法的城市需要更广泛考虑的一点：技术和行政结构可能不同，但一个有效的投诉处理系统需要可及的渠道、明确的职责以及坚持到底的承诺。超越热线。对北京来说，挑战不仅在于接收投诉并作出回应。

目标日益在于利用数百万件诉求所产生的信息来识别反复出现的问题、改善公共服务，并在问题引发更多投诉之前加以解决。根据市政府的2025年报告，自改革开始以来的七年间，北京报告其解决率从53.1%上升到97.3%，而满意率从64.6%上升到97.7%。这些数字有助于说明这条热线的发展及其在城市治理方式中的核心作用。我午夜与12345的接触，是与一个非常庞大系统的一次小小互动。我打电话是因为我想知道我为什么一直睡不着。

有人倾听了，找到了相关信息，给我回了电话，并给了我一个答复。对某位居民在某个夜晚来说，这就足够了。但该系统的更大意义在于，当数百万次这样的互动被收集、评估并用于为决策提供依据时会发生什么。北京的经验为了解中国以人为本的治理逻辑提供了一个出人意料地具有揭示性的窗口，同时提出了与其他地方城市相关的问题：居民如何让自己的关切被听到？公共机构如何有效回应？

又如何利用个别投诉中的经验教训来防止类似问题再次发生？归根结底，良好的治理始于倾听人民，通过解决他们的问题而受到检验，并通过改善他们的生活而获得合法性。编者按：Zaruhi Poghosyan是CGTN Digital的多媒体编辑。本文是关于北京不断发展的、面向本地居民和国际访客的数字服务系列文章的一部分。

articles.title: China's growth offers opportunity over shock, experts say
articles.titleCn: 专家称中国增长带来的是机遇而非冲击
articles.summary: After four days touring the frontlines of China's economic evolution, from Xinyu, an age-old manufacturing hub reinventing itself with advanced industries, to the bustling entrepreneurial engine of Wenzhou, the cradle of the country's private sector, a group of former international political leaders and scholars converged in Beijing on Sunday for the Mingde Strategic Dialogue 2026.
articles.summaryCn: 多国前政要与学者在北京明德战略对话2026上表示，中国高质量发展为世界经济提供稳定器，西方应欢迎而非以保护主义抵制中国企业的全球化。

paragraphs.en: After four days touring the frontlines of China's economic evolution, from manufacturing hub Xinyu to entrepreneurial engine Wenzhou, a group of former international political leaders and scholars {{0}} in Beijing on Sunday for the Mingde Strategic Dialogue 2026. Joining their Chinese {{1}} for the third edition of the event hosted by Renmin University's Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies, the group gathered under the theme "{{2}} and Vitality: New Opportunities China's Development Brings to the World" to discuss where the world's second-largest economy is headed and what it means for global growth. Former Ethiopian President Mulatu Teshome, the first from the visiting delegation to take the floor, set an optimistic tone for the dialogue. "The global economy is searching for silver linings, and today China's high-quality development is providing exactly that, helping serve as a {{3}} for the world economy," Teshome said. China is {{4}} the global green shift through mass electric vehicles (EVs) {{5}}, widening Global South trade corridors and offering zero-tariff access to some, and {{6}} supply chains through advanced manufacturing and digital innovation, he further explained.
paragraphs.cn: 在为期四天走访中国经济发展前沿——从制造业重镇新余到创业引擎温州——之后，一群前国际政要和学者于周日齐聚北京，参加明德战略对话2026。他们与中国同行一道参加由中国人民大学重阳金融研究院主办的第三届活动，围绕“韧性与活力：中国发展带给世界的新机遇”这一主题，探讨世界第二大经济体将走向何方以及这对全球增长意味着什么。埃塞俄比亚前总统穆拉图·特肖梅是来访代表团中第一位发言的人，他为对话定下了乐观的基调。“全球经济正在寻找一线希望，而今天中国的高质量发展恰恰提供了这一点，有助于成为世界经济的稳定器，”特肖梅说。他进一步解释说，中国正通过大规模采用电动汽车、拓宽全球南方贸易走廊、向部分国家提供零关税准入，以及通过先进制造业和数字创新重新定义供应链，加速推动全球绿色转型。

paragraphs.en: Days ago on a single ride from his hotel to an airport in Shanghai, the former president conducted a personal {{7}} along the highway: 240 green license plates reserved for new energy vehicles against just 27 traditional blue ones, real-time evidence of China's adoption of clean technology. Chinese high-tech advances, particularly in EVs, present a {{8}} opportunity for developing nations like Ethiopia, which now bans diesel vehicle imports to adopt {{9}}, eco-friendly EVs that cut oil import needs, Teshome told CGTN. Moreover, Teshome {{10}} that Chinese vehicles now exceed many {{11}} Western equivalents in quality, offering strong {{12}} appeal, modern design, comfort and styling for global consumers. "The industrial achievements which China has had, we take it as an opportunity, not as a challenge, not as a threat," he told CGTN on the sidelines of the dialogue. Former Ethiopian President Mulatu Teshome takes an interview on the sidelines of the Mingde Strategic Dialogue 2026 in Beijing, China, October 11, 2026.
paragraphs.cn: 几天前，这位前总统在从酒店前往上海某机场的一趟车程中，沿高速公路做了一次个人统计：240块专为新能源汽车保留的绿色车牌，而传统蓝色车牌仅有27块，这是中国采用清洁技术的实时证据。特肖梅对CGTN表示，中国的高科技进步，尤其是在电动汽车领域，为像埃塞俄比亚这样的发展中国家提供了至关重要的机遇——埃塞俄比亚现已禁止进口柴油车，以采用价格可负担、环保的电动汽车，从而减少石油进口需求。此外，特肖梅强调，中国汽车目前在质量上已超过许多西方传统同类产品，为全球消费者提供了强大的美学吸引力、现代设计、舒适性和造型。“中国取得的工业成就，我们把它视为机遇，而不是挑战，不是威胁，”他在对话间隙对CGTN说。2026年10月11日，埃塞俄比亚前总统穆拉图·特肖梅在中国北京明德战略对话2026期间接受采访。

paragraphs.en:
Yet, while developing nations view China's industrial expansion as a {{13}} for their own economic transitions, some Western capitals have increasingly signaled alarm. This {{14}} in global perspective became a central focus during the afternoon sessions, where attendees turned their attention to a seemingly growing wave of trade {{15}} erected against Chinese exports. Addressing the dialogue, George Galloway, a former member of Parliament of the United Kingdom, argued that this {{16}} reflects a political double standard. He pointed out that some economies {{17}} frame China's normal export activities as "overcapacity" to {{18}} trade restrictions under the banner of "de-risking."
"We used to call it exports when we were overproducing," Galloway told the attendees. "It was merely exports."
To underline the historic {{19}}, he drew a direct parallel to the industrial revolution: "Britain was once quite the 'overproducer' itself, and we loved that.
paragraphs.cn: 然而，尽管发展中国家将中国的产业扩张视为自身经济转型的催化剂，一些西方国家的政府却日益发出警报。这种全球视角的分歧成为下午会议的核心焦点，与会者将注意力转向似乎日益高涨的针对中国出口的贸易壁垒浪潮。英国前议员乔治·加洛韦在对话中发言，认为这种反弹反映了一种政治双重标准。他指出，一些经济体刻意将中国的正常出口活动定性为“产能过剩”，以便打着“去风险”的旗号为其贸易限制辩护。

paragraphs.en: But we don't love it when the shoe is on the other foot," he quipped. Galloway went on to criticize the apparent Western pivot away from traditional capitalist logic and free-market principles it used to hold dear. "The belief in free trade, and the belief that the market is king, and that the consumer is king – all of these things are {{20}} in the interests of {{21}} and the protest against overproduction," he observed. Responding directly to these Western friction points, Chinese economists at the forum offered a systematic defense of the nation's industrial path, reframing China's rapid technological ascendance as a structural rebalancing of the global economy. Tu Xinquan, dean of the China Institute for WTO Studies at University of International Business and Economics, pushed back against Western narratives that accuse China of shocking the global trading system.
paragraphs.cn: “我们过去在自己生产过剩时把它叫做出口，”加洛韦对与会者说。“那不过是出口而已。”为了强调这种历史讽刺，他直接类比工业革命：“英国曾经自己就是十足的‘生产过剩者’，而我们当时很喜欢那样。但轮到别人时我们就不喜欢了，”他打趣道。加洛韦接着批评西方明显背离了它曾珍视的传统资本主义逻辑和自由市场原则。“对自由贸易的信念，对市场为王、消费者为王的信念——所有这些都被抛弃了，取而代之的是保护主义和对生产过剩的抗议，”他评论道。针对这些西方摩擦点，与会的中国经济学家系统性地为中国产业道路辩护，将中国技术的迅速崛起重新定义为全球经济的结构性再平衡。对外经济贸易大学中国WTO研究院院长屠新泉反驳了西方指责中国冲击全球贸易体系的说法。

paragraphs.en: In reality, Tu argued, Western anxieties stem from Chinese enterprises breaking long-held {{22}} through genuine technological breakthroughs. Rather than shutting doors, he noted, Western economies should welcome Chinese firms going global, a necessary step toward resolving global {{23}} and stabilizing supply chains. In hard economic math, former Vice Minister of Finance Zhu Guangyao quantified the sheer {{24}} of opportunity awaiting international businesses during China's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030). After four days touring the frontlines of China's economic evolution, from manufacturing hub Xinyu to entrepreneurial engine Wenzhou, a group of former international political leaders and scholars converged in Beijing on Sunday for the Mingde Strategic Dialogue 2026.
Joining their Chinese counterparts for the third edition of the event hosted by Renmin University's Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies, the group gathered under the theme "Resilience and Vitality: New Opportunities China's Development Brings to the World" to discuss where the world's second-largest economy is headed and what it means for global growth.
Former Ethiopian President Mulatu Teshome, the first from the visiting delegation to take the floor, set an optimistic tone for the dialogue.
"The global economy is searching for silver linings, and today China's high-quality development is providing exactly that, helping serve as a stabilizer for the world economy," Teshome said.
China is accelerating the global green shift through mass electric vehicles (EVs) adoption, widening Global South trade corridors and offering zero-tariff access to some, and redefining supply chains through advanced manufacturing and digital innovation, he further explained.
Days ago on a single ride from his hotel to an airport in Shanghai, the former president conducted a personal tally along the highway: 240 green license plates reserved for new energy vehicles against just 27 traditional blue ones, real-time evidence of China's adoption of clean technology.
Chinese high-tech advances, particularly in EVs, present a vital opportunity for developing nations like Ethiopia, which now bans diesel vehicle imports to adopt affordable, eco-friendly EVs that cut oil import needs, Teshome told CGTN.
Moreover, Teshome highlighted that Chinese vehicles now exceed many legacy Western equivalents in quality, offering strong aesthetic appeal, modern design, comfort and styling for global consumers.
"The industrial achievements which China has had, we take it as an opportunity, not as a challenge, not as a threat," he told CGTN on the sidelines of the dialogue.
Former Ethiopian President Mulatu Teshome takes an interview on the sidelines of the Mingde Strategic Dialogue 2026 in Beijing, China, October 11, 2026. 
Yet, while developing nations view China's industrial expansion as a catalyst for their own economic transitions, some Western capitals have increasingly signaled alarm. This divergence in global perspective became a central focus during the afternoon sessions, where attendees turned their attention to a seemingly growing wave of trade barriers erected against Chinese exports.
Addressing the dialogue, George Galloway, a former member of Parliament of the United Kingdom, argued that this backlash reflects a political double standard. He pointed out that some economies deliberately frame China's normal export activities as "overcapacity" to justify trade restrictions under the banner of "de-risking."
"We used to call it exports when we were overproducing," Galloway told the attendees. "It was merely exports."
To underline the historic irony, he drew a direct parallel to the industrial revolution: "Britain was once quite the 'overproducer' itself, and we loved that. But we don't love it when the shoe is on the other foot," he quipped.
Galloway went on to criticize the apparent Western pivot away from traditional capitalist logic and free-market principles it used to hold dear.
"The belief in free trade, and the belief that the market is king, and that the consumer is king – all of these things are abandoned in the interests of protectionism and the protest against overproduction," he observed.
Responding directly to these Western friction points, Chinese economists at the forum offered a systematic defense of the nation's industrial path, reframing China's rapid technological ascendance as a structural rebalancing of the global economy.
Tu Xinquan, dean of the China Institute for WTO Studies at University of International Business and Economics, pushed back against Western narratives that accuse China of shocking the global trading system.
In reality, Tu argued, Western anxieties stem from Chinese enterprises breaking long-held monopolies through genuine technological breakthroughs.
Rather than shutting doors, he noted, Western economies should welcome Chinese firms going global, a necessary step toward resolving global imbalances and stabilizing supply chains.
In hard economic math, former Vice Minister of Finance Zhu Guangyao quantified the sheer magnitude of opportunity awaiting international businesses during China's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030).

That incremental growth alone, Zhu stressed, exceeds the total annual GDP of Germany, the largest economy in Europe, that stood at more than $5 trillion in 2025.

A complaints hotline can do more than resolve individual complaints. It can show a government what's going wrong everywhere, and help it fix that too, according to Ondrej Dostal, a Czech member of the European Parliament (MEP).
Speaking to CGTN at the 2026 Beijing Forum on Swift Response to Public Complaints, Dostal said Beijing's 12345 hotline has lessons for European cities trying to improve public services and build trust with citizens.
He said the gap between the rights people have and the services they can actually access is one of the biggest challenges in government. A hotline like 12345, he said, could close that gap by putting citizens in touch with the right department, and by giving authorities a clearer picture of what people are complaining about.
"If we had similar mechanisms, it would very much help common people to really get the services they need without unnecessary hassle," Dostal said, adding that a system like this could also give people a more direct tool in how they're governed.
Technology should help governments listen
Dostal said Beijing's 12345 hotline shows how digital tools can turn individual complaints into a wider picture of what a city needs. By collecting and analyzing large volumes of complaints, AI can help officials spot recurring problems and inform policy decisions.
"Technology cannot rule. People have to decide what will happen," he said. "But technology like AI can streamline the process of finding new ideas or agreeing on solutions to problems."
He said these tools could be particularly useful in Europe, where administrative responsibilities are spread across many institutions and levels of government. Citizens often have to navigate complicated paperwork or rely on personal connections to get things done. AI could help identify the procedures that aren't working and make it easier for officials to help people quickly.
From responding to preventing problems
Dostal said the bigger lesson was that governments shouldn't just respond to complaints. They should look for patterns, and prevent problems before they arise. Analyzing complaints could help authorities target healthcare and social care better, and spot everyday environmental problems.
Beijing's approach cannot be directly replicated across Europe, he said – populations, legal systems and administrative structures are different. Still, he said its focus on coordination, digital tools and anticipating public needs offers useful lessons.
For Dostal, more responsive governance depends not simply on adopting new technology, but on ensuring that it helps people get what they need.

(ECNS) -- The 47th World Congress of Vine and Wine and the 24th General Assembly of the International Organisation of Vine and Wine (OIV) are being held in Yinchuan, northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, from Monday to Friday, alongside the sixth China (Ningxia) International Wine Culture and Tourism Expo.
At a lifestyle market in the exhibition area, the aroma of coffee mingled with the fruity notes of wine, while food stalls, art installations and stamp-collecting activities contributed to the lively atmosphere.
"Traditional trade fairs mainly target industry players and professional buyers. We hope to break down barriers and bring wine out of wineries and professional exhibition halls and into people's everyday lives," said Li Jun, head of the Administrative Committee of the Ningxia Helan Mountain Eastern Foothills Wine Industry Park.
The lifestyle market caters to everyday consumers, helping address a gap in efforts to develop a broader consumer base for wine, Li said.
Innovative offerings at the market are making wine more approachable. Bartenders have crafted signature cocktails using wines from the eastern foothills of the Helan Mountains, bringing out fruity, berry-like notes while reducing tannic astringency to make the drinks more appealing to newcomers.
The market also offers wines suited to different levels of experience, from easy-drinking, fruit-forward options for beginners to more complex selections for seasoned drinkers, along with tastings of unblended wines.
For many wineries, it was their first time participating in a lifestyle market of this kind.
Moving beyond traditional business-to-business trade fairs, they had an opportunity to engage directly with everyday consumers and showcase a livelier, more approachable side of wines from the eastern foothills of the Helan Mountains in Ningxia.
The eastern foothills of the Helan Mountains in Ningxia have emerged as one of China's major wine-producing regions, where favorable climate and soil conditions have supported the industry's growth.
By the end of 2025, Ningxia had 40,467 hectares of land planted with wine grapes or designated for their cultivation, accounting for roughly 40% of China's total, according to local authorities.

articles.fullText:
A White House task force on artificial intelligence will assess the technology's risks and opportunities, while preventing overregulation that stifles innovation, its leader Jay Clayton has told the Wall Street Journal.
Clayton, the US director of national intelligence, is widely reported to be the new AI czar in the administration of US President Donald Trump, though the appointment is yet to be confirmed.
Clayton would become the second person to hold the informal title after venture capitalist David Sacks, who held the role at the start of Trump's second term before stepping down.
The new "Super Intelligence Force" – using Trump's preferred term for artificial intelligence – will have 120 days to report on the risks and opportunities of the technology, the Journal reported on Saturday.
"The president asked that a group be put together that was going to ensure exactly what he said... (that) we stay the leaders in superintelligence, and that the interests of the American people are put first," Clayton said.
"The risk of not being first is high," he added.
"Not being first increases the identified, and unidentified, risks, particularly from our adversaries. Being first will better enable us to address those risks on behalf of the American people."
A longtime Wall Street lawyer, Clayton represented Goldman Sachs during the 2008 financial crisis and Barclays in its purchase of Lehman Brothers' assets.
Trump tapped Clayton to lead federal prosecutors in Manhattan at the start of his second term, and the Senate confirmed him as intelligence chief in July.
He has no background in the tech industry.
The task force's charter states that it will "develop plans for responding to SI-enabled threats to our society, while preventing overregulation and regulatory capture that would stifle innovation and competition," according to the Journal.
It will also "recommend ways to improve the government's response capacity under existing authorities."
Members of the task force include Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
